key_insight: K/Rb-based lead-free double perovskites β2SnGeX6 (X = Cl, Br, I) are structurally stable, ductile, and strongly tunable from wide- to narrow-bandgap semiconductors for photovoltaics and thermoelectrics.
engineering_relevance: These materials offer a non-toxic platform for solar absorbers, tandem/NIR optoelectronics, and high-temperature waste-heat recovery, with composition selection controlling bandgap and ZT.
method: DFT-based study of structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties
Stability screening using formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor
Elastic constants, band structures, and transport/phonon-related analysis to assess device suitability
evidence_signal: The abstract reports all six compounds are thermodynamically stable and cubic, with direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 to 0.64 eV and a peak ZT of 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: The highest thermoelectric performance is predicted at elevated temperature and from first-principles modeling, so experimental synthesis, phase stability, and defect effects still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
